exposure: orofacial cleft status (all, isolated, or nonisolated)
cohort: The study included 25,879,282 live births registered in the U.S. Vital Statistics Natality Birth Data.
finding: Newborns with orofacial clefts exhibited an increased prevalence of poor birth health outcomes, including lower birth weight, lower Apgar 5 scores, prematurity, and more abnormal conditions at birth.
mod_finding: Newborns with orofacial clefts were found to be more susceptible to being born by cesarean section.
